text:
Jacob Fowler stopped 33 of 34 shots, and the Canadiens needed every one of them to leave Winnipeg with a win. By our numbers, he saved 2.8 goals more than the quality of those shots deserved, which is the gap between a goalie having a good night and stealing a game. Fowler was drafted 69th overall in 2023 and came to Montreal by way of Boston College, where he posted a .940 save percentage in 2024-25. On Sunday he made the same kind of numbers count against the NHL's best.

Montreal scored twice in the second period, and both goals came on the rush of a stretch where the Canadiens were the better team. Lane Hutson, the 2022 second-round pick out of the U.S. U-18 program, opened the scoring at 7:19 from Noah Dobson and Cole Caufield. Kaiden Guhle doubled it at 11:04 on a shot we gave a 1% chance of going in. Winnipeg answered only at 15:24 of the third, when Isak Rosen snapped one home to make it 2-1.

The rest of the game belonged to the Jets. They out-attempted Montreal 73 to 57, put 34 shots on goal to 21, and carried a 3.84 to 2.98 edge in expected goals, the measure of chance quality. We gave them a 63% chance of winning if the game were replayed from every shot, against 37% for Montreal. They also went 0 for 4 on the power play, with 1.42 expected goals from those chances. Mark Scheifele alone put seven shots on net.

For Winnipeg, the loss makes it five straight without a win (0-3-2). Stuart Skinner stopped 19 of 21 and faced shots worth 2.98 goals, so the problem was finishing, not goaltending. Montreal takes the two points with its goalie as the reason.
